newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel steady despite India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel steady despite India.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices were steady to slightly softer on Monday despite India's meagre award of 90,000 tonnes in its tender for September, traders said.

They said the low award has already been taken into account on Friday when swaps prices started to fall but rose earlier in the day amid concerns of tight supplies and higher prices in Northwest Europe due to shutdowns of cat-crackers at three refineries.
Swaps prices for August quoted as high as $22.60/$22.75 before slipping to $22.55/$22.65 in late trading, up 10 cents from Friday.

A 150,000-barrel physical gas oil cargo was sold by a European major oil company at $22.50 per barrel for August 19-23 lifting free-on-board basis to a Singapore trader. This was 35 cents below the last deal on Tuesday.
A US major offered for the same lifting period at $22.80, while a Mediterranean trader offered for August 21-25 lifting at $22.60.
A U.S. oil and power company made a bid for late August lifting at $22.00 but was untraded as the level was deemed too low, traders said.
The Philippines Petron Corp's second tender in a row closed late on Monday and is valid for a day. The latest tender for 20,000 tonnes of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil is for early September delivery.
Petron had awarded an earlier tender for August 10-20 delivery to a South Korean refiner.

Traders said the additional gas oil requirements might be due to an unscheduled shutdown of a 15,000-barrel-per-day thermal cracker and a scheduled maintenance at a crude unit and a reformermer in September 1-12.
Jet fuel was offered higher at $23.50 by a European major, up from $23.00-$23.15 on Friday, but attracted no bids.
Traders said a MidEast oil company last week sold 30,000 tonnes of jet fuel at five cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes to a major for second half August delivery, cost-and-freight basis.
